entries.content: He (c-1) In John, the personal pronoun, generally emphatic in Greek where inserted, is used so constantly that it can hardly be considered such in many cases, but certain instances which are considered to be more definitely emphatic are given in italics. The same spirit of emphasis causes the very frequent use of ekeinos for the third person ('he,' 'they,' &c.). Its sense is 'that,' contrasted with 'this,' and hence is emphatic; as 'that man' in English, sometimes having the sense of 'such a one as that.' A number of cases where this word also is used emphatically have also been indicated.
men. (d-12) This latter is a reciprocal proposition, i.e. it can also he read 'the light of men was the life.'
from (e-6) Para, with genitive, 'from with,' see v. 14, Note d.
lightens (f-11) Or 'is light to every man.' Not 'enlightens,' but 'sheds its light upon.'
own, (g-5) Or, 'what was his own,' but the neuter is used by John in the most general way for persons.
right (h-12) Exousia. 'right to take that place.' see Matt. 10.1. children (a-15) Teknon. see Note, Mark 7.27. on (b-22) Eis. see Note. 2Tim. 1.12.

dwelt (c-7) Lit. 'tabernacled.' with (d-22) para, with a genitive as here, means 'on the part of;' 'from with' gives the sense. But this must not be understood in the sense of 'with' merely. It has not this significance in the New Testament.

subsists (e-11) Ginomai, 'has come,' that which, not having actually been in being before (i.e. in the world), now begins to be so. So the Word was (v. 1), but everything else 'began to be.' The world 'had its being,' 'began to be,' through Him (v. 10). He 'became flesh' (v. 14), ginomai. So 'grace and truth came into being.' I am not satisfied with 'subsists,' but 'came' gives the idea of coming into the world. No doubt they did so, but the word has not this force. They began to exist de facto down here. The verb is singular, and 'grace and truth' go together in the person of Christ. Nothing subsisted by the law, it was a rule given; but grace and truth actually commenced to be, not in God's mind of course, but in revelation and actual existence down here. But its so taking place supposes its continuance.
in (f-14) Eis, not en. perhaps 'on.' The expression indicates the place where, or the state. see Acts 8.23; Mark 1.9. In chap. 13 it is en in ver. 23, epi in ver. 25.
Lord, (g-19) 'Lord' has no article here, which is irregular in Greek, but I do not doubt it is in place of the name 'Jehovah,' as in other Gospels. prophet. (h-24) Isa. 40.3.
stands, (i-14) Lit. 'has taken his place as stands.' see Gen. 18.2; Rev. 3.20.
abode; (a-15) Lit. 'abides.'
at (b-9) i.e. 'looking carefully;' so ver. 36; Matt. 19.26; Luke 22.61. stone). (c-27) Or 'Peter.'
come (d-9) Lit. 'Can there be any good thing.'
was, (a-19) Lit. 'is.'
on (b-19) Eis. see Note, 2Tim. 1.12.
temple (c-6) Hieron, as Matt. 4.5.
both (d-16) Or 'and.'
written, (e-8) Ps. 69.9.
temple, (f-9) Naos. The house itself -- the shrine.
temple (f-11) Naos. The house itself -- the shrine.
temple (f-6) Naos. The house itself -- the shrine.
on (b-15) Eis. see Note, 2Tim. 1.12.
knew (g-15) Epiginosko, a strong word meaning 'to know well' or 'recognise,' as Matt. 7.16, &c.
anew (h-18) Not only 'again,' but 'entirely afresh,' as from a new source of life and point of departure; translated in Luke 1.3, 'from the origin.' It is a new source and beginning of life.

on (a-16) Eis, as in ver. 36; chs. 4.39; 6.29,35,40. so (b-3) I have hesitated a moment whether 'so' referred to the kind of love that gives 'eternal life,' which is mentioned in verse 15, and is the great subject of John, in contrast with all earthly blessings and favour. The sense then would thus be, that he has loved men in view of eternal life, 'so that' he has given, &c. (See 'so,' Acts 14. 1.) When followed by 'that,' the regular force of the Greek is, 'so much that.' whosoever (c-14) Lit. 'every one who,' as ver. 15.

are; (d-26) Elenko. to show the true character of anything, so as to convict, and hence reprove by showing a man's fault. It is used in chs. 8.46, 'convinces;' 16.8, 'bring demonstration;' Eph. 5.11,13, 'reprove' and 'expose.'
heart (e-22) Lit. 'rejoices with joy.'
earth (a-16) Or 'is from the earth.' The sense is 'having by nature his origin' here below, he is of and belongs to the earth. 'Of' (ek) is characteristic.
received (b-4) Or 'receives.' it is the aorist, 'has received,' not referring to time, but to the fact. hence perhaps 'receives' is as well.

on (d-4) Eis. see Note, 2Tim. 1.12. subject (e-15) Or 'believes not on.' It is the obedience of submission to his person, not practical obedience to his commands, whatever proof this may be of the other; but it is not exactly the same thing as believing on him as an object revealed in grace. see Note, Heb. 3.18.

fountain (f-3) Another word is used for the 'well,' ver. 11, in which the spring was; and this word, translated 'fountain,' is used for what springs up as life in the renewed man. was (g-22) Lit. 'thus.' see 1Cor. 7.26, 'so as he is' and Note, 2Pet. 3.4.

ever, (h-16) 'Never thirst for ever' is a little awkward, but 'never thirst' is too vague; it may be to our minds much as a present thing for this life. The expression is strong in negation, and expresses lasting for ever. see chs. 8.51,52; 10.28; 11.26; 13.8.
worshipped (a-3) Proskuneo, and so to ver. 24. see Matt 4.10.
hour (b-9) Or 'an hour,' as ch. 5.25,28, and see Note, 1John 2.18.
hour (b-3) Or 'an hour,' as ch. 5.25,28, and see Note, 1John 2.18.
spirit; (c-4) Or 'God [is] spirit.'
not (a-14) A strengthened negative.
child (b-11) The diminutive, but not in ver. 51.
servants (c-9) Or 'bondmen,' doulos.
sheepgate, (d-8) Neh. 3.1.
away, (e-16) Or 'withdrawn.'
loves (a-4) Phileo, not as ch. 3.35. see Notes, chs. 11.3 and 21.15.
hour (b-9) See 1John 2.18.
hour (b-7) See 1John 2.18.
practised (c-8) done (c-18) Poieo, and Prasso; see Rom 1.32.
shining (d-6) Lit. 'appearing,' as ch. 1.5; 1John 2.8.
shape, (e-27) As 'form,' 'fashion;' Luke 3.22; 9.29.
search (f-2) Or 'Search.' Not command, but appeal. witness (g-21) Or 'are the witness-bearers.'
you. (a-14) Lit. 'yourselves.'
alone? (b-20) Or 'from the only God.'
mountain, (c-7) The mountain country. see Note, Matt. 5.1.
men (d-6) Anthropos. 'mankind.' men (e-18) Aner. 'men' in contrast to women. see Matt. 14.21; 1Cor. 11.3.
men (d-2) Anthropos. 'mankind.'
to (f-8) Or 'about to.'
on (a-16) Eis. see Note, 2Tim. 1.12.
written, (b-12) Ps. 78.24 and Neh, 9.15.
of (c-12) Ek. see Note, ch. 3.31.
on (a-24) Eis. see Note, 2Tim. 1.12. never (d-18) never (d-27) A strengthened negative. The words, 'at any time,' apply to both clauses.
All (e-1) Lit. 'whatever.'
from (f-6) Some authorities read 'out of' -- ek.
on (a-18) Eis. see Note, 2Tim. 1.12. sees (g-13) Or 'beholds' (theoreo), as ver. 62, chs. 7.3; 8.51; 12.45; 14.17,19; 16.16.

prophets, (h-6) Isa. 54.13. from (a-20) Para with a genitive (as 'of' God, ver. 46). It is what is received directly from the Father. I add 'himself' that its immediateness may be felt, which is the point of the sentence.
of (b-13) Para with genitive. 'from with.'
flesh (c-14) Or 'give us flesh.'
eats (d-3) Present participle. so in vers. 56,57,58. It is characteristic. he is the 'eater' of this divine food.

account (e-12) account (e-25) Dia with the accusative is not simply 'by' or 'through,' and here it is evident that it is important to be accurate. The sense is 'by reason of what the Father is and his living;' 'I live by reason of his being and living.'
Will (f-7) Not simply the act, but the will to do it. 'Is it your will or disposition?' 'Do ye also wish to go away?'
on (a-7) Eis. so vers. 31,38,39,48. see Note, 2Tim. 1.12.
temple (b-16) Hieron. as Matt. 4.5.
gave (c-3) Or 'wonder because of this. Moses gave.' that (d-7) Or 'because' and omit ( ).
judge (e-7) Aorist, and with the article. Lit. 'have judged the righteous judgment.'
know (f-7) Oida. 'conscious knowledge.' see Note, 1Cor. 8.1. knows (g-21) Ginosko. objective knowledge.
temple, (b-7) Hieron. as Matt. 4.5. know (f-13) know (f-17) know. (f-39) Oida. 'conscious knowledge.' see Note, 1Cor. 8.1.
know (f-2) Oida. 'conscious knowledge.' see Note, 1Cor. 8.1.
dispersion (a-27) * i.e. 'Jews scattered.'
believes (b-3) Pres. participle, i.e. characteristic.
word, (c-10) Logos. see Heb. 6.1.
there. (a-28) Lit. 'being in the midst.'
know (b-20) Oida, as ver. 19; ch. 7.29. come (c-34) Present tense and characteristic. see Note h, Gal. 2.14.
true. (d-16) Deut. 17.6 and 19.15.
from (e-8) from (e-12) Ek. see Note, ch. 3.31; lit. 'of those things which are.'
Altogether (f-14) 'in the principle and universality of what I am;' i.e. his speech presented himself, being the truth.
know (g-4) Ginosko. see Note, 1Cor. 8.1.
word (a-16) Logos. see Heb. 6.1.
do (b-13) poieo; usually 'practise' (see ch. 5.29), but it hardly suits here or in vers. 39,40; still it refers to habitually or characteristically doing, not a mere act.
do (b-2) poieo; usually 'practise' (see ch. 5.29), but it hardly suits here or in vers. 39,40; still it refers to habitually or characteristically doing, not a mere act.
word. (a-13) Logos. see Heb. 6.1.
of (c-3) of (c-46) Ek. see Note, ch. 3.31. stood (d-29) Perfect tense. what has been and continues.
word, (a-13) Logos. see Heb. 6.1. never (e-16) See Note, ch. 4.14.
never (e-32) See Note, ch. 4.14.
word. (a-33) Logos. see Heb. 6.1. know (f-3) Objective knowledge, ginosko. know (g-8) Conscious knowledge, oida, three times here.
authority (a-16) Exousia. right to act as well as power. Hence used for magistracy. see Matt. 10.1. of (b-34) Para with gen.. see ch. 6.45.
Mary (d-4) Or 'But [the] Mary was she who,' &c.
loved (b-3) Agapao, as ch. 3.35.
Didymus, (c-4) Or 'twin.'
stadia (d-8) About two miles.
ask (e-10) Aiteo. see Note a, ch. 14.16.
never (f-11) See ch. 4.14.

moved (a-18) Or 'groaned.' Elsewhere only in Matt. 9.30; Mark 1.43; 14.5, translated, 'sharply charged,' 'spoke very angrily.' Here it was inward feeling (in spirit) produced by the deep pain caused by seeing the power of death over the human spirit. There was so far indignation that there was deep antagonism to the power of evil and Satan in death. It may be 'groaned' is the best word. troubled, (b-23) Tarasso; or 'shuddered,' as ch. 12.27; 13.21.
wept. (c-2) Lit. 'shed tears;' only used here; not as Luke 19.41, &c.

moved (a-5) Or 'groaned.' Elsewhere only in Matt. 9.30; Mark 1.43; 14.5, translated, 'sharply charged,' 'spoke very angrily.' Here it was inward feeling (in spirit) produced by the deep pain caused by seeing the power of death over the human spirit. There was so far indignation that there was deep antagonism to the power of evil and Satan in death. It may be 'groaned' is the best word.
was, (a-18) Lit. 'is.'
pure (b-10) Or 'liquid;' a word difficult of interpretation, but most likely 'pure.' see Note, Mark 14.3.
burial; (c-17) i.e. it was now the time. see ch. 19.40. The word is used in Gen. 50.2 (LXX) for embalmment in Hebrew.
was (a-11) Lit. 'is.'
on (d-13) Eis. see Note, 2Tim. 1.12.
Israel. (e-28) See Ps. 118.26.
written, (f-14) See Zech. 9.9.
because (g-10) Or 'that.'
worship (h-14) Proskuneo. see Matt. 4.10.
overtake (a-25) The sense is 'overtake so as to seize upon,' as Mark 9.18, 1Thess. 5.4.
in (b-7) Eis. see ver. 11.
on (b-14) Eis. see ver. 11.
fulfilled, (c-13) See Isa. 53.1.
again, (d-11) See Isa. 6.9-10.
on (b-10) Eis. see ver. 11.
God. (e-11) Lit. 'the glory of men ... the glory of God.'
on (b-9) on (b-13) Eis. see ver. 11.
beholds (f-4) As ch. 6.40.
on (b-14) Eis. see ver. 11.
end. (a-39) 'To the end' does not give the full force, for it makes it refer to time; whereas going through with everything is implied.
during (b-2) Or 'being finished.'
going (c-23) Lit. 'goes.'
know (d-13) The first 'know' is conscious, the second objective. see Note, 1Cor. 8.1.
over (e-10) 'Washing applied to the whole body;' the second 'wash' is a different word meaning 'to wash hands or feet.'
bondman (f-8) See Note, Matt. 10.24. sent (g-17) Lit. 'apostle.'
fulfilled, (h-20) See Ps. 41.9.
now (i-5) 'From this present time.' He had not told them previously thus; 'now' ('henceforth,' ch. 14.7), is a point of time from or to which time is counted.
spoke. (k-12) Lit. 'speaks.' so in ver. 24.
in (l-10) 'in,' here, is en, 'on,' ver. 25, is epi.
is (a-10) is (a-18) Lit. 'has been.'
be (a-3) Lit. 'has been.'
Children (b-1) Teknia. diminutive; an affectionate term, as 1John 2.1,12,28.
on (c-9) on (c-13) Eis. see Note, 2Tim. 1.12.
know (d-3) know (d-9) Oida. as ch. 7.29.
know (d-7) know (d-16) Oida. as ch. 7.29.
henceforth (e-14) As 'now,' ch. 13.19.
on (c-10) Eis. see Note, 2Tim. 1.12.

beg (a-4) In the latter chapters of John's Gospel, in order to maintain the distinction, frequently important, between erotao and aiteo, the first is translated 'demand' [except John 14.16 (beg)], the second 'ask.' There are times when they may be used indiscriminately, at other times each has a sense peculiar to itself. erotao expressing a familiar request to a person where intimacy exists [or equality, either assumed or actual]; aiteo, the request rather for something by an inferior to his superior. The disciples employ both of these words in their relations with Jesus, but only aiteo with relation to the Father. In his relations with his Father, Jesus employs erotao but not aiteo. Martha uses aiteo in ch. 11.22. For the difference between the two, compare John 16.23. In ch. 14.16 the word is erotao; in vers. 13 and 14 aiteo. Comforter, (b-13) One who carries on the cause of any one and helps him. This Christ did on earth; this (1John 2.1) he does now in heaven, and the Holy Spirit on earth 'manages our cause, our affairs, for us.' If 'solicitor' were not too common, it just answers the sense.
know (c-17) know (c-21) Objective knowledge. see Note, 1Cor. 8.1.
know (c-6) Objective knowledge. see Note, 1Cor. 8.1.
ask (a-14) Aiteo. see Note a, ch. 14.16.

this (b-2) 'In this' refers to what follows. no one, I think, can be familiar with John's writings and doubt it. Thus the Father is glorified and they become disciples of his. mine. (c-18) Perhaps more exactly, 'In this will my Father have been glorified that ye have borne much fruit, and ye will have become,' &c.
of (d-31) Para with gen.. see Note a, ch. 6.45.
know (e-6) Or 'ye know;' objective knowledge.
bondman (f-10) Doulos. see Note, Matt. 10.24.
cause. (g-17) 'Gratuitously,' 'freely,' 'for nothing,' Ps. 35.19 and 69.4.
from (h-13) with (h-24) Para with gen.. see Note d, ch. 1.14.
offended. (a-13) Verb from skandalon. see Note, Matt. 13.57.
service (b-24) 'Service' here is priestly service, latreia.
demands (c-15) Erotao. see Note, ch. 14.16.

demonstration (d-7) Elenko. 'convince' supposes effect in the person convinced; 'convict' would not do for righteousness or judgment. I have said 'bring demonstration,' though it suggests perhaps too much the action of the Spirit when come; but his presence and all that he does affords this demonstration. see ch. 3.20.
on (e-8) Eis. see Note, 2Tim. 1.12.
announce (f-36) The Greek has the sense of 'reporting,' 'bringing back a report.' Here I conceive because it is a message brought from another.
announce (f-13) The Greek has the sense of 'reporting,' 'bringing back a report.' Here I conceive because it is a message brought from another.
announce (f-23) The Greek has the sense of 'reporting,' 'bringing back a report.' Here I conceive because it is a message brought from another.
demand (c-8) Erotao. see Note, ch. 14.16.
ye (g-20) Or 'ye indeed.'
child (h-20) Paidion, as ch. 21.5.
demand (a-7) Erotao. see Note, ch. 14.16. ask (b-20) Aiteo. see Note, ch. 14.16. you. (c-29) Or 'ask the Father, he will give you in my name.'
full. (d-19) Or 'fulfilled,' as ch. 17.13.
declare (e-26) As 'announce' in ver. 13.
demand (a-19) Erotao. see Note, ch. 14.16.
affection (f-6) affection (f-13) Phileo. see Notes, chs. 11.3 and 21.15. from (g-23) Para, with gen.. see Notes, chs. 1.14; 6.45; 15.26.
authority (h-6) Exousia. see Note a, ch. 10.18.
the (i-4) I add the article, because it throws the emphasis on 'eternal,' as in the Greek.
with (k-8) with (k-17) 'Along with' as to presence and place.
manifested (l-3) Phanero, as chs. 2.11; 9.3; 21.1,14.
words (m-3) Rhema, the divine communications, see Note, v. 14. known (n-20) Objective knowledge.
perdition, (a-31) 'Perished' and 'perdition' are verb and noun from one Greek root. they show what Judas belonged to.
word, (b-6) Logos. the word of God in testimony, see 1Cor. 1.5, distinct from Rhema, the divine communications, ver. 8.
word (b-7) Logos. the word of God in testimony, see 1Cor. 1.5, distinct from Rhema, the divine communications, ver. 8.
by (c-13) Or 'in' or 'in the power of truth.' En. see Matt. 3.11.
on (d-15) Eis. see Note, 2Tim. 1.12.
Father, (e-2) Or 'of the world righteous Father! -- And,' &c.
chiliarch, (a-6) Strictly, 'the commander of a thousand men' (a military tribune).
praetorium; (b-9) See Note a, Matt. 27.27.
says, (a-30) See Ps. 22.18.
it, (b-21) Probably means, 'binding it to hyssop.'
bears (c-6) Both verbs, 'saw' and 'bears,' are in the perfect tense, expressing what was present in the mind of the writer. knows (d-15) Oida, as ch. 7.29.
fulfilled, (e-11) See Ex. 12.46; Ps. 34.20.
says, (a-5) See Zech. 12.10.
burial. (b-28) See ch. 12.7.
attached, (c-18) Phileo. see ch. 11.3.
Rabboni, (d-14) See Mark 10.51, the only other instance of the use of this word.
Didymus, (a-8) Or 'twin.'
not (b-48) 'In no wise.' a strong negative.
know (c-16) Oida, see Note at 1Cor. 8.1.
Children, (d-6) Paidion, the diminutive. as 1John 2.13,18, 'little children.'
knowing (a-20) Oida, see Note at 1Cor. 8.1.

knowest (a-28) Oida, see Note at 1Cor. 8.1. lovest (b-15) to (b-33) This passage (vers. 15-17) illustrates the force of two Greek words for 'to love,' phileo and agapao. The former signifies the love of friendship, and is more intimate and intense. It is here translated 'I am attached to,' and in ch. 16.27 'have affection for.' Agapao, more often used in the New Testament, is more general, and signifies love as the settled disposition of a person rather than as an emotion. It is used for God's love to man (except in Titus 3.4, where a compound word is used which embodies the word phileo) and for the love of men to God. Both words are used for the love of the Father for the Son, phileo once only, John 5.20, and agapao in John 3.35, &c.. and for the love of Christ for his own, phileo in John 11.3 and agapao in John 11.5 and elsewhere. Phileo is used in John 16.27, of the love of the Father for the disciples, and of the love of the disciples for Christ.
knowest (a-23) Oida, see Note at 1Cor. 8.1.
knowest (a-39) Oida, see Note at 1Cor. 8.1. knowest (c-43) Objective knowledge.
him, (d-3) Lit. 'this [one].'
know (a-19) Oida, see Note at 1Cor. 8.1.
